scenes.card: Zeus sends Hermes, the gods' messenger, flying over the sea to Calypso's island with the order to release Odysseus.

subs.text: Book five.
Odysseus—Nymph and Shipwreck.
Scene one.
Hermes Carries the Decree.
Dawn rises, and the gods sit again in council —
Athena counting aloud the sorrows of Odysseus in the nymph's halls, and the ambush laid at sea against his son.
Hermes, my son, our messenger as always —
go to the nymph of the braided hair and speak my fixed decree:
Odysseus goes home.
No god beside him, no mortal ship —
on a lashed raft he shall come, through hardship, to Scheria on the twentieth day.
Hermes straps on his sandals, takes his wand, and skims across the sea.
Hermes reaches Ogygia, enters Calypso's fragrant cavern, and finds her weaving at the fire.

scenes.title: Calypso Receives the Order
scenes.card: Calypso protests that the gods resent goddesses who love mortal men, but she agrees to let Odysseus go.

subs.text: Scene two.
Calypso Receives the Order.
Hermes of the golden wand —
an honored guest, and a rare one.
Sit, and let me set ambrosia and red nectar before you.
What errand brings you across so much salt water?
Speak it;
my heart says do it, if it can be done.
You ask, goddess, and I answer truly:
Zeus sent me —
who would cross this waste of brine for pleasure?
He says you keep here the most ill-fated of all the men who fought at Troy,
and that it is not his doom to die far from his people.
Send him quickly, and do not wake the Thunderer's anger against you.
Calypso denounces the gods' jealousy toward goddesses who love mortal men.
It was I who saved him when Zeus's bolt split his ship in the wine-dark sea —
but so be it, since Zeus commands.
Let him go.
Only I cannot send him:
I have no ships, no oarsmen —
my counsel he shall have, freely and unhidden, that he may come home unharmed.

scenes.title: Odysseus Distrusts Freedom
scenes.card: Odysseus suspects a trick until Calypso swears an oath; offered immortality with her, he still longs for his wife.

subs.text: Scene three.
Odysseus Distrusts Freedom.
Unhappy man, weep here no longer —
I am ready now to let you go.
Rise;
cut long timbers and build yourself a broad raft, and I will stock her with bread and water and red wine,
and send a fair wind behind you for home.
Calypso suspects a trap and demands a binding oath that she will not plan his ruin.
Then witness Earth, and the wide Heaven above, and the down-dripping water of Styx —
the greatest oath the blessed gods can swear:
I plot no ruin against you.
I counsel you only as I would counsel my own heart.
Immortality with her surpasses Penelope.
Goddess and queen, do not be angry —
I know it all:
wise Penelope must fade beside you, for she is mortal and you are deathless.
Even so, every day I long for home and the hour of my return.
And if some god wrecks me again on the wine-dark water, I will endure that too —
my heart is old in suffering.

scenes.title: Building the Raft
scenes.card: With tools from Calypso, Odysseus builds a raft in four days, and she sends him off with food and a fair wind.

subs.text: Scene four.
Building the Raft.
Here at the island's edge the tall trees stand —
alder and poplar and sky-high fir, long dry, that will ride light on the water.
Take the great bronze axe and the adze;
here is cloth for a sail and cord to lace her.
Build, and I will bring all the rest.
Calypso fells, trims, bores, joins, decks, and fences the timbers over four days.
Calypso rigs mast, yard, sail, steering oar, and ballast.
Calypso bathes and clothes him, loads food and water, and sends a warm wind behind the raft.

subs.text: Scene five.
Poseidon Breaks the Sea.
For seventeen days Odysseus steers by the stars until Scheria rises ahead.
So —
the gods changed their minds about Odysseus while I feasted far away.
Yet even now I will give him his fill of trouble.
A toppling sea takes the raft broadside —
she spins, the mast cracks, and the whole frame rolls.
Odysseus is swept away and barely regains it.
Abandon the raft and swim.
Athena restrains the winds except the north wind that drives him shoreward.

sign.name: Originary world
sign.operation: Wide, black sky and a heaving brick sea, the raft small; low camera at water level when the wave rolls it.

scenes.world: A black storm sea under low cloud, heaving swells and spray, a small raft alone in it; silent-era and newsreel storm footage, no land but a dark headland.

captain.asks: A wide black sky over heaving sea with the raft small, then the camera at water level as the wave rolls it: an originary, elemental world.
diagnosis: The sea footage is uniformly bw storm stock: the world holds better here than anywhere in the books.
Odysseus has no face: the man at the oar, on the headland, in the water are all absent or a blur.
Water-skiers and rapids kayakers lurk on the row; steering off them keeps the elemental world clean.

scenes.title: The River Accepts the Castaway
scenes.card: After two days swimming, Odysseus finds a calm river mouth, crawls ashore on an unknown land, and sleeps under leaves.

subs.text: Scene six.
The River Accepts the Castaway.
Odysseus swims for two nights and days while waves hurl him toward a reef-lined coast.
Athena shows him a river mouth free of rocks and wind.
Hear me, lord of this stream, whoever you are —
I come to your current a suppliant, fleeing Poseidon's anger out of the sea.
Even the deathless gods respect a wandering man who comes in need;
pity me, lord, for I claim that mercy now.
Odysseus returns Ino's veil to the sea, crawls ashore, and hides beneath two intertwined olive bushes.
Odysseus buries himself in leaves and Athena seals him in sleep.

sign.name: Figure of enfeeblement
sign.operation: Extreme wide from the cliffs: the head a few pixels among the surf lines, the reef white; pull back.

scenes.world: A reef-lined coast of white surf and cliffs, a quiet river mouth among reeds and two olive bushes, overcast light to evening; documentary coastal look.

captain.asks: Extreme wide from the cliffs, the castaway a few pixels in the surf, then pull back: a figure of enfeeblement, the man almost erased.
diagnosis: Coast and river are well supplied: surf, cliffs and still water hold the documentary coastal world.
The enfeebled body is almost never there; the one swimmer is a colour bather, the crawl is borrowed from another reel.
The olive bushes and leaf bed are missing; ploughed fields and garden flowerbeds stand in and break the place.

prologue: Now we meet Odysseus himself, held for years on a remote island by Calypso, a goddess who loves him and wants him to stay. The gods order her to let him go. He must cross the sea alone, and the sea god Poseidon still hates him.
